committed.question: Which ten non-test functions or methods are called from the most call sites in non-test code?
committed.evidence: Count resolved direct call sites (call_kind 'direct') whose caller and callee are both outside test files. Ties are broken by symbol id.
committed.SQL:
SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS call_sites
FROM code.calls c
JOIN code.symbols s ON s.symbol_id = c.callee_symbol_id
JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id
JOIN code.symbols cs ON cs.symbol_id = c.caller_symbol_id
JOIN code.files cf ON cf.file_id = cs.file_id
WHERE c.call_kind = 'direct'
  AND s.kind IN ('function', 'method')
  AND NOT f.is_test AND NOT cf.is_test
GROUP BY s.symbol_id
ORDER BY call_sites DESC, s.symbol_id
LIMIT 10;

ORDER BY call_sites DESC, s.symbol_id
LIMIT 10;

committed.question: What share of direct call sites could the static analysis resolve, by resolution kind?
committed.evidence: Direct call sites have call_kind 'direct'; callback rows are references passed as arguments and are not call sites.
committed.SQL:
SELECT resolution, COUNT(*) AS calls,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM code.calls WHERE call_kind = 'direct'), 1) AS pct
FROM code.calls
WHERE call_kind = 'direct'
GROUP BY resolution
ORDER BY calls DESC, resolution;
committed.answer: dynamic_attribute, 11794, 37.8; external, 5430, 17.4; imported, 4848, 15.5; same_file, 4352, 14.0; builtin, 4163, 13.4; unresolved, 349, 1.1; method_on_self, 242, 0.8

committed: Only Python files are analysed; other languages in the repository are not represented.
Dynamic imports (importlib, __import__) and imports executed through strings are not resolved.

Internal callees are resolved only through plain dotted names: same-file definitions, import bindings (following re-exports up to 3 levels), and self/cls methods of the enclosing class. Every other call keeps a null callee and is classified, never guessed: builtin (an unshadowed builtin name), external (rooted in a non-internal import or a module-level name assigned from one), dynamic_attribute (a method on an object whose type this analysis does not infer), or unresolved (parameters, local callables, super() and anything left).

Functions passed by reference are recorded as call_kind callback (low confidence) only when a plain dotted name appears directly as a positional or keyword argument of a call inside a function and resolves, by the same rules, to an internal function or method: asyncio.to_thread(f, x), loop.run_in_executor(None, f), executor.submit(f), Thread(target=f), functools.partial(f), Depends(f). References held in lists, dicts, assignments, return values or decorators without a call are not recorded, a name the enclosing function binds locally is skipped, properties passed as values are skipped, arguments of inspect.* and of builtins that only examine a value (getattr, isinstance, print, repr and the like) are skipped, and every other receiving call is assumed, not proven, to invoke the reference.
Builtin classification does not see local variables or parameters that shadow a builtin name.
Inherited methods resolve only when the base class is statically resolvable to a definition in the repository; such calls are marked low confidence.
Local variables that shadow a module-level name are not tracked, so a shadowed call may resolve to the module-level definition.
Nested functions and classes defined inside a function are not symbols; their calls are attributed to the enclosing symbol.
Test links are static: a test that exercises a file without importing it, and without a matching file name, is not linked.
Descriptions and summaries are verbatim docstring text; no description is generated or inferred.
Calls at module level, outside any function or class, are not recorded (1046 in this snapshot).
3 module names are shared by several files (e.g. top-level test modules); imports of those names are not resolved.

Dynamic imports (importlib, __import__) and imports executed through strings are not resolved.

Internal callees are resolved only through plain dotted names: same-file definitions, import bindings (following re-exports up to 3 levels), and self/cls methods of the enclosing class. Every other call keeps a null callee and is classified, never guessed: builtin (an unshadowed builtin name), external (rooted in a non-internal import or a module-level name assigned from one), dynamic_attribute (a method on an object whose type this analysis does not infer), or unresolved (parameters, local callables, super() and anything left).

Functions passed by reference are recorded as call_kind callback (low confidence) only when a plain dotted name appears directly as a positional or keyword argument of a call inside a function and resolves, by the same rules, to an internal function or method: asyncio.to_thread(f, x), loop.run_in_executor(None, f), executor.submit(f), Thread(target=f), functools.partial(f), Depends(f). References held in lists, dicts, assignments, return values or decorators without a call are not recorded, a name the enclosing function binds locally is skipped, properties passed as values are skipped, arguments of inspect.* and of builtins that only examine a value (getattr, isinstance, print, repr and the like) are skipped, and every other receiving call is assumed, not proven, to invoke the reference.
Builtin classification does not see local variables or parameters that shadow a builtin name.
Inherited methods resolve only when the base class is statically resolvable to a definition in the repository; such calls are marked low confidence.

Imports inside a function, method or class bind only in that body. Other local variables that shadow a module-level name are not tracked, so a shadowed call may resolve to the module-level definition.

Nested functions and classes defined inside a function are not symbols. Calls in their decorators and defaults, and in a nested class body, are attributed to the enclosing symbol, which runs them. Calls inside a nested function body are attributed to it only when it calls the nested function or passes it on by name, directly or through other nested functions; otherwise they are not recorded.
Test links are static: a test that exercises a file without importing it, and without a matching file name, is not linked.
Descriptions and summaries are verbatim docstring text; no description is generated or inferred.
Calls at module level, outside any function or class, are not recorded (1046 in this snapshot).
Calls inside nested functions that the enclosing function never calls or passes on by name (handlers it registers, closures it returns) are not recorded as its calls (229 in this snapshot).
3 module names are shared by several files (e.g. top-level test modules); imports of those names are not resolved.
